concepts.name: the Wald interval for a proportion
concepts.formula: p̂ ± z·√( p̂(1−p̂)/n ), with p̂ = k/n successes in n trials

concepts.name: the Wilson score interval
concepts.citation: Wilson (1927), Journal of the American Statistical Association 22(158), 209–212

concepts.name: coverage of a nominal 95 per cent interval
concepts.slide: Definition — coverage, and what a half-width costs
concepts.formula: coverage(p, n) = (1/R)·Σ_{r=1}^{R} 1{ low_r ≤ p ≤ high_r }

concepts.name: the labels a stated half-width costs
concepts.slide: Definition — coverage, and what a half-width costs
concepts.formula: n = ⌈ 0.25·(z/h)² ⌉ at the worst case p = ½

concepts.name: Shannon entropy
concepts.formula: H(P) = −Σ_i P(i)·log P(i)

concepts.name: cross-entropy
concepts.formula: H(P,Q) = −Σ_i P(i)·log Q(i)

concepts.name: the Kullback–Leibler divergence
concepts.formula: D(P ‖ Q) = Σ_i P(i)·log( P(i) / Q(i) ) = H(P,Q) − H(P), in nats
concepts.citation: Kullback & Leibler (1951), Annals of Mathematical Statistics 22(1), 79–86

concepts.name: Jensen's inequality
concepts.formula: f( E[X] ) ≤ E[ f(X) ] for convex f, with equality only where f is straight or X never varies

concepts.name: the symmetrised index, Jeffreys' divergence
concepts.formula: J(P,Q) = Σ_i ( P(i) − Q(i) )·log( P(i) / Q(i) ) = D(P‖Q) + D(Q‖P)
concepts.citation: Jeffreys (1946), Proceedings of the Royal Society A 186, 453–461

concepts.name: the index's noise floor at a stated bin count
concepts.formula: floor(B) = median over R resamples of J( reference, resample of the reference ) at B bins
concepts.citation: Yurdakul & Naranjo (2020), Journal of Risk Model Validation 14(4), 89–100

concepts.name: the materiality threshold, derived from the measured floor
concepts.slide: Definition — the materiality threshold, derived from the floor
concepts.formula: threshold(B, q) = Quantile_q { J( reference, resample of the reference ) at B bins }, over the same R resamples
concepts.citation: Yurdakul & Naranjo (2020), Journal of Risk Model Validation 14(4), 89–100

concepts.name: the Wasserstein-1 distance
concepts.formula: W₁(P,Q) = ∫ |F_P(x) − F_Q(x)| dx = ∫₀¹ |F_P⁻¹(u) − F_Q⁻¹(u)| du
concepts.citation: Vallender (1974), Theory of Probability and Its Applications 18(4), 784–786

concepts.name: the two binnings inside compare_four
concepts.slide: Definition — the two binnings inside compare_four
concepts.formula: H and D: equal-width edges over both samples · J: the reference's quantile edges, opened at both ends

concepts.name: the standardised shift, Glass's Δ
concepts.slide: Definition — the standardised shift, and the rule it is read against
concepts.formula: Δ = ( mean_current − mean_reference ) / s_reference, ddof = 1

concepts.name: the rule a shift is called material by, with a derived index bound
concepts.slide: Definition — the standardised shift, and the rule it is read against
concepts.formula: material when |Δ| ≥ 2.0 or J ≥ threshold(B, q) derived from this feature's own null

concepts.name: the positive control on a null result
concepts.formula: verdict( reference, current + k·s_reference ) must return material, with k stated beside the result
concepts.citation: Saltelli et al. (2019), Environmental Modelling and Software 114, 29–39

concepts.name: the detection limit of the verdict on the target
concepts.formula: detection limit = min{ k in the swept sizes : verdict( reference, current + j·s_reference ) is material for every swept j ≥ k }

concepts.name: the drift verdict, and the three calls it may make
concepts.slide: Definition — the drift verdict, and the three calls it may make
concepts.formula: act if the target is material; watch if its index is unmeasurable, or the control did not fire, or its index is above the floor; no material change only when the index is at or below the measured floor and the control fired
concepts.citation: Saltelli et al. (2019), Environmental Modelling and Software 114, 29–39

concepts.name: the classifier two-sample test
concepts.formula: the two samples differ when the interval around a held-out classifier's accuracy lies above chance, chance = 1/2 on balanced classes
concepts.citation: Rabanser, Günnemann & Lipton (2019), Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32

concepts.name: Welch's t-test
concepts.slide: Definition — Welch's t-test, and the bootstrap to the reading grain
concepts.formula: t = ( m₁ − m₂ ) / √( s₁²/n₁ + s₂²/n₂ )

concepts.name: the bootstrap that changes only the sample size
concepts.slide: Definition — Welch's t-test, and the bootstrap to the reading grain
concepts.formula: the same difference resampled with replacement to n readings, seed 20200122

concepts.name: Cohen's d
concepts.formula: d = ( m₁ − m₂ ) / s_pooled, s_pooled = √( ((n₁−1)s₁² + (n₂−1)s₂²) / (n₁+n₂−2) )
concepts.citation: Cohen (1988), Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences
